title: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

sense.text:
A fool is a person who lacks good sense, judgment or wisdom: an idiot, a simpleton, a dolt, a nincompoop, a blockhead, a nitwit, a buffoon, a clown. That is a strong word, but that is what a fool is. You know it ain't right and you are about to make an awful, horrible decision, but because you are in love you go with it anyway, blinders on. And in the scripture a fool is not just somebody who is dumb. A fool is somebody who despises God's wisdom and instruction.

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge.” To fear God is to know that he created you, gave you purpose and told you what to do. That is the first step of having knowledge of God. Many of our people have no fear of God in them; it is nowhere to be found. That is why they don't search, they don't look, they don't seek out the Lord. They go with the social norms, with whatever the world is doing, and live their lives like that.

“But fools despise wisdom and instruction.” That is the definition of a fool. Wisdom comes from the scriptures and from the Lord, and the Lord has put men in your life who have been through things and had to apply the scriptures to those situations. When they bring those scriptures to you, it is so you can make the proper decision. But the fool says, he's trying to ruin my life, he don't want to see me get married, he don't want to see me happy. No. They are trying to warn you, guide you and lead you according to the Bible so that you don't make a devastating mistake.

“My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.” What are your father and mother supposed to be telling you? Thus saith the Lord. And what are your fathers in this truth telling you? Thus saith the Lord.

“For they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck.” When you listen to the instruction of your father and your mother in this truth, it empowers you and keeps you away from things you don't want to deal with. It helps you, molds you, builds you and puts you in a better place than you would have been if you didn't listen.

The chains about thy neck are there to restrain you from doing something stupid. That is what instruction does for you. But when a fool despises instruction, all hell breaks loose.

precepts.why:
What is your purpose? To fear God and keep his commandments. “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.”

That is the whole duty of man, and that is the first thing you learn. When you fear God, that is the first step of knowledge: God made me, so I have to do what he said to do. That is “the fear of the Lord” that “is the beginning of knowledge.”

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The things written aforetime are the word of God. “That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The Bible is a book of instruction, and through it we gain hope and understanding. We know the things that are to come. We have the cheat book: we win the fight at the end of the day. Remember the almanac in Back to the Future? He thought he was doing something. We have the greatest almanac to hit the world, the word of God.

How would we be the children of God if we did not come to the Bible to gain understanding and wisdom, and more importantly to learn how to apply the words of God in our present-day lives? What would be the difference between us and the folks in church who hold the Bible in their hand in front of the pastor but take no instruction from it? Nothing. We have the Bible so we know how to move. I live like this because the word said to do it.

They say, you Israelites don't think for yourselves. You're damn right I don't. I let the word of God dictate my thoughts, and when something comes in that ain't according to the word of God, I have to fight it, block it out and do what God said. That's the fight. Meanwhile the world does whatever the hell they want to do.

Today's class is about proving and picking a spouse: asking the right questions and paying attention to all the red flags and all the signs. If you don't, because you're out here love drunk, there will be hell to pay.

“What is heavier than lead? and what is the name thereof, but a fool?” To be a fool is like carrying heavy lead on your back. It is burdensome. Everything in your life is harder. You know that person who always wants to do things the hard way, who always has to bump his head and mess up to get it, instead of taking counsel? Somebody tells him there's something down that road, so go this way. Oh no, he wants to go down there and find out.

“Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, than a man without understanding.” Why make something so difficult? Because you don't want to listen. Because you think you know what you're talking about.

There is the one who always thinks he has the answers: nobody's telling me what to do, I've got to figure it out. And there is a worse one, the one who acts like he wants counsel. He asks all the questions, takes notes, says hold on Deacon, say that again slow, acts like he's hanging on every word. We went from the alpha to the omega, sat up there for hours, covered every step. And then he turns around and does the exact opposite. That is a man without understanding, and he is heavier to bear than sand, salt and iron.

“There is a way which seemeth right unto a man.” Because you think you know what to do. I'm grown. They don't understand my situation. They ain't walked a mile in these shoes. You think you're dealing with something no man has ever dealt with, like it's not common to man, like you're from space. And the worst part is when the one saying it is half your age and hasn't lived half your life.

“But the end thereof are the ways of death.” You believe everything you're saying, you just know the outcome, you have more understanding than those before you. Not realizing that the end of your decision is going to be the death of you. That death comes in many forms and fashions. It may not be instant. It could be a lifetime of heartache, pain, even bloodshed.

Counsel is given from the experiences that have been seen. A man should not counsel on what he does not know; he sends you to somebody who has dealt with it. Either way, you should be seeking counsel, not sitting up trying to figure things out on your own.

In proving: you decided to prove this sister, she decided to prove you, you've been talking a while, and it might feel right and feel good. But all the signs are there and you are ignoring them, caught up in the moment. Seven, eight months or a year from now you will pretend to be surprised, but everything you needed to know was put right in front of you. Many relationships feel right but are spiritually wrong. You need discernment. Proving is the process of finding out whether this man or woman is who God sent for you. This isn't a credit check for a vehicle; it is much more important than that, and if you don't pay attention you will play yourself.

Sisters, the man you choose will be your head, your lord, your boss. He will tell you what to do, when and how, and he has more power than your daddy had. You're not going to go through the vetting process to make sure he ain't crazy? Do not confuse the stages of attraction for love: infatuation, lust, emotional dependency, the honeymoon phase where everybody sends their representative, projection, comfort and routine, possession and control, and trauma bonding. None of them is love.

In the honeymoon phase both people are on their best behavior, the real personalities are hidden, no real testing has happened, and blatant red flags are disregarded. You got evicted? They be tripping sometimes. You got fired? The devil's a liar.

“The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way.” The wisdom a prudent person has is to understand his way. You might feel some type of way about the person, but you are not going to blatantly disregard red flags, and you are not going to be hasty to credit, because wisdom is present in someone that's prudent.

“But the folly of fools is deceit.” There is no understanding in the fool, and his folly is deceitful: he tells himself it really ain't that bad. Must have been for the Lord, we going to be tried and go through tribulation. Not realizing this person is a bum and he is ignoring the red flags. It goes both ways, man and woman. You cannot let your simplicity deceive you just because you feel some type of way about somebody.

In this truth people have disregarded blatant red flags, like the STD test. She was supposed to get it done but something happened with her insurance, six, seven months and always a reason. You were so worried about laying down with the sister you did not give a damn that she didn't take the test, and you wake up with the bump. Love hasn't been proven until it's been tested.

Projection is being in love with your own ideas. You give a person attributes they never present, fill in the blanks and build a version of them in your mind, ignoring who they actually show you they are. The brother can't save a penny, but in your mind he's a trust fund baby. He got evicted from the first complex because they found his Bible, from the second because they saw him in purple and gold, from the third because the devil is a liar, while all your leaders and the brothers you fellowship with pay their bills and keep their places. It's never his fault: a lack of accountability. He says surely he's oppressed and spoiled evermore, and you believed him. Or you fall for potential instead of reality: he is always finna, about to, gonna, the multi-million dollar business and the cryptocurrency about to pop off. From a father's perspective, that all sounds good, but before he gets my daughter's hand he has to be in the seat, doing what he said he would do. You're currently a bum. You can't have my daughter.

Bishop Yawsaw has been reaching out because this is happening all over the nation. A sister was asked whether she and the brother had shown each other their STD test results, and she said, I trust him. I don't trust nobody but the Lord.

“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man.” Miss me with the trust. I trust God. “And maketh flesh his arm”: you make another human being your strength, the one you rely on and believe in. Hell no. I need to see the test.

In this present world there need to be multiple tests, and you need to go to the hospital with them, because people have had AI make them an STD chart. If you ain't doing nothing, you ain't got nothing to hide. But if you're nasty, now you're scared, running from the truth. It is a red flag if someone doesn't want to go get tested. What have you got to hide?

You are in a relationship with an illusion, not a person. You believed his lies, you believed her lies, and that is not the person you are really dealing with. You want the wedding with the sun shining and the wind blowing in your dress or your cape, and mess around and it be a thunderstorm that day, because you didn't do right.

Comfort and routine get mistaken for love. After a year of proving and talking every day you are used to each other, and the fear of starting over keeps you there. Hell no, you don't have to make it work. You have to find the person God created for you. Your adversary the devil is a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour, and somebody may have been sent your way to destroy you.

“I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness.” Solomon went deep to find out the levels of wickedness. He did a diligent search to understand how deep this really goes. And when he understood it, watch the first thing he deals with.

“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets.” Out of all he searched and sought out, he found something more bitter than dying. There are people who are a trap: Satan sends them your way. Snares and nets are traps set to destroy and to kill. King Solomon said it is worse than dying to be trapped with an individual like that.

“And her hands as bands”: to destroy you in any and every way possible. Everything you try to be great in, she sabotages.

“Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her.” That man will escape. Satan sent her your way, but she wasn't your forever; she wasn't the person God sent for you. The damn devil tried to take you out. “But the sinner shall be taken by her.” That is his portion: a wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man.

So never fear starting over. When you look back after making the right decision, you will be proud of yourself. Look back after the wrong one and think about all the time lost in turmoil, pain and heartache because you got somebody whose hands are as bands. And the spark is supposed to still be there while you are proving. If you are not even married yet and it is already dimming, and you only stay because it is a habit and you don't want to start over, the signs are there.

This is what we just got through talking about. In the you're-mine stage, jealousy and control get mistaken for care, and when a brother senses others are interested a competitive spirit steps in and he rushes to take her off the market. That is not your spouse yet: you are just proving. You are in the interviewing stage, an investigator trying to find out the truth, and everybody don't just come out and tell you they're crazy. You have to look, listen and pay attention; the signs are always there. And trauma bonding, connecting through shared wounds and trauma stories instead of Christ and the truth, is not love: y'all are just bleeding on each other.

“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” You give in to the red flags, to false perceptions you created or misperceived, thinking it's this or that when it's not, all because you want to fulfill whatever that lust is. And the lust may be for marriage itself: I want a wife, I want to be on the cabin trip with the married men, I want to be at the Marriage Is Honorable event. So you rush the process, overlook things and ignore the signs God put in front of you. A year later you're at the cabin trip all right, crying and depressed, the topic of the cabin trip, because you did not go through the proper process. Lust will do that.

“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” See the process, all because you couldn't control yourself.

Everybody has a plan before the fight: drop back, duck, roll, uppercut. Then you get punched in the face. Lust is like that. In here we are all talking big, but when you are put in the situation, that's when you find out if you are battle tested. That is when you have to draw on the understanding you have been given: let's slow down, let's do it how we're supposed to, let me talk to somebody, I think I'm about to do something stupid.

An example of lust. “Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her. And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar.” This is evil as hell: this is his own sister. He let his lust drive him crazy. If you think your lust ain't going to drive you crazy, you're already crazy.

“Jonadab was a very subtil man.” Jonadab is the devil as well. Amnon had the devil on him, and the devil came to give him ill advice. That happens many times: the person you go to, who is supposed to give you godly counsel, tells you how to be the devil.

The king thinks his son is sick and needs help, but all he wants is his sister. They have different mothers and the same father, and he is lusting after her to the point that he devised this whole plan to lay with her. Lust is a powerful drug, a powerful demon. Israelites read things like this and say that's white folks' stuff, but this happened in Israel, in King David's house.

“Come lie with me, my sister.” And she answered, “Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.” It is filth; it is not supposed to happen in the nation of Israel. “As for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel.” Then she tries to get herself out of the situation: “speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.”
“Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice.” Why? That lust demon was on him. “But, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.”

“Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her.” That is the clarity that comes after. The demon left, the lust jumped off him, and reality hit. He knew what he had committed, and now he hates her.

The exact same thing happens once you make a hasty decision. Like buying a car and feeling a certain way afterward, but this ain't a car, it's marriage, and you can't test drive the wife. After the sex, all the understanding comes back and you realize how stupid you were. Now the house is in shambles, the arguments never stop, and the regret comes too late.

Brothers, be careful. Sisters, be even more careful. “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” Her beauty causes men to overlook all the red flags, all the flaws, all the things wrong with her, and everything he could have dodged, or waited a little longer and corrected, before he went into the marriage.

“A man is brought to a piece of bread.” When you go into the marriage you have to have things established already: boundaries in place and clear communication on expectations. Go into it trying to wing it and what comes out is chaos in the home. There is never peace; every day is war and a battle, and you are in it depressed and mad at the world because of your own decision, because you couldn't wait and do it the right way.

The worst thing any man in this truth can do is marry the wrong woman. You can be the strongest brother in the scriptures, the strongest teacher, and the wrong woman can destroy your spirit. Two believers can't divorce, so you have to work it out, and good luck working it out with a stubborn, inconsiderate, halfway-believing Israelite who doesn't fear God or instruction. The brother pulls up to the house and sits in the car because it's hell inside. All the signs were showing the forecast, like the low clouds before rain, but you couldn't discern it.

There is responsibility once you pull the trigger. A marriage built on sex, secrecy, rushing and no counsel is bound to have problems. The way you establish your marriage in the beginning affects its trajectory for years to come. A back-door marriage increases the probability of problems a hundredfold.

Secrecy looks like this: in front of everyone, we've been proving for a year. In reality, phone sex for eight months, sexting, some even laying together, every time saying it won't happen again, and saying nothing to leadership. Then you tie the knot and everybody says, good job brother, you waited. You devil, you didn't wait. So don't be surprised when that spouse keeps other secrets from you. She kept secrets very well when y'all were doing that; she is keeping them from you now. You saw that attribute when he tried you, and you let your lust take you into it. And some, once they are linked together, ghost leadership the entire proving stage, an update every seven or eight months, and then only come back when the marriage is at its boiling point.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” When you lay down with a woman you have an obligation. We don't go around having casual sex. Entice means to deceive: he deceived her. Some brothers kick it: all it took was, dang girl, you fine, and the drawers fell off. Bam. You simple.

“If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” With sex comes responsibility. The man who enticed her and lay with her has to make her his wife; anything other than that is fornication.

precepts.why:
“Flee fornication.” To flee is to run. Sisters, if he tries to do anything or allude to anything, run. Brothers, if she is trying anything, flee. You don't want to be called a fornicator.

Not every situation where a person has sex is marriage. If it ain't marriage, it is fornication. You can be proving, not ready to marry, let your lust take over, and in your simple mind think, well, I guess this is my wife now. No, you just committed fornication, because that wasn't the woman God has for you. You want to make it right? Then you find out three years later she doesn't even believe, she commits adultery on you, and she wasn't your forever: she was your hasty decision. Why not take your time and wait? Finding out the hard way is what a fool does.

sense.text: “Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.” When you are quick to do something, the haste brings about sin. You don't process, you ain't thinking, and that is how you fall into the midst of sin. When you are not locked in and tuned in to what's going on around you, you will make lifelong decisions based on short-term gratification. You jump straight into sex and now you are trapped. You have to think it through.

“Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof.” The beginning is hard: you have to be patient, go through the anxiety of wondering whether this is the right person, cross your t's and dot your i's. But when you did it right, were patient, took counsel, didn't jump the gun and asked the right questions, the end of all that is a good thing. If you didn't, the whole tenure is miserable from beginning to end.

“And the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.” Being patient in spirit is taking your time and knowing it's going to be all right; there's no need to rush the process, the Lord's got you. Some of you have been single for years with discipline, and the moment somebody shows interest you are ready to throw it away in a few weeks. That ain't nothing but Satan.

Be real with yourself and your situation. Know your limitations when proving: what's going to get you caught up, what's going to get you put out the body. Don't play with that.

“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” If you know yourself, you know your limitations and your borders, and then you are ready to prove someone else. I'm not going that far; if I see this, it's a done deal. I hear clearly that this is what he wants and that's not me, so let me end this now, no big deal, let's move on. Instead of trying to force it and hoping that if you never bring it up again, he won't want it anymore. It's going to come back.

What we teach here is unheard of in the world, where people move in together after a couple of weeks, and she just posts up and never leaves.

“If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first.” If you prove a friend, how much more a wife or a husband? That's why we call it proving. “And be not hasty to credit him.” What comes out of hastiness? Sin, back-door marriages. You opened your legs up, sis: you were hasty. Bro, you were hasty, and you gave her all the credit. Then brothers think, I've got to marry her now, go get the paperwork. No, negro, you just committed fornication, and both of y'all need to go out the body. We have never forced a marriage on anybody because they had sex. Not every man that lay with a woman in the Bible had a wife; it was fornication, and whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

“For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of thy trouble.” You wonder why she dipped. The moment things got hard, we're eating ramen, she's back at her daddy's house. Brothers stand up and say, I drive trucks, I make this much money, and the sister thinks, let me get with him. Then when times get hard she bounces, because she wanted you for what you had and you didn't see the signs.

“And there is a friend, who being turned to enmity and strife will discover thy reproach.” We've seen it in marriages gone bad: the wife leaves and has a whole video about you and your nasty ass drawers: this negro did this, he do that, there's something wrong with him, he got erectile dysfunction. All your business is out there because she turned to enmity on you. Why? You didn't prove her.

“Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of thy affliction. But in thy prosperity he will be as thyself, and will be bold over thy servants. If thou be brought low, he will be against thee, and will hide himself from thy face. Separate thyself from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends.” All of this is done through proving. The signs are right in front of your face; you just ignore them and don't want to accept them.

“Prove all things.” Not some things: all things. You have to do a thorough investigation, especially with marriage, because you don't know what he's got going on in his head. Sisters, look at his phone. If he gets to twitching when you ask, that's nasty. And the same goes for the other side of the room. The DMs, the text messages: check a phone and you may find the person you say you are proving is a totally different individual.

“A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.” How do you know a woman is contentious? She gainsays you all the time. You give instructions and she adds her two cents when it isn't needed. Everything's a fight; you can't have a conversation without it turning into something. You ask what she wants to eat and it ends with, don't call me no more: what, you think I'm fat? Men can be contentious as well.

See the signs before marriage. If you love war, there are warmongers out there for you, but nobody goes into a marriage wanting to argue until they hate each other. On the phone while proving you can hang up and not talk for a day or two. Married, you see each other every day. Every red flag you see before marriage is heightened a thousand times after it. But because of your lust, you will ignore all of those red flags.

You have had all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. When something is said to you, you can say, hold on, I'll call you back, and ask somebody, does this sound right? But for some reason everybody is grown. You're not in your right mind.

“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your soul is a job. Leadership isn't about sitting up front and getting their plates first. There are things you never see or hear about because things are put in place: the men deal with the men, and the leaders' phones are the first to get called. The senior sisters deal with the sisters. There should not be any brothers counseling the women; congregational matters the senior sisters bring up, and if somebody has to be judged it is dealt with that way. That senior sister or senior brother will tell you, no, that don't sound right, that's not wise, and a lot of situations are avoided.

precepts.why: “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don't follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it. That is why there are those set over you who watch for your souls.

“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” Do nothing without advice. Sisters, the blueprint has been given to you: the things to look for when it comes to men. Take the advice of those who watch for your soul before you act, and you will not have to repent of what you did.

sense.text:
When looking for a husband, ask: does this man have stability, does he have discipline?

“He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He has no rule over his spirit; he isn't stable. How is he going to take care of you? He isn't mentally sound, blown about with every wind of doctrine, always bringing out something brand new, little dumb breakdowns that didn't come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag, sister: run.

Sisters, spiritually you should never aim down; aim up. You want a man with more understanding than you, who can build you up, lead and guide you. If you've been in this truth for years and you're the one teaching a novice to wear his fringes every day, and you made him your husband, you will lose respect for him and go somewhere else for understanding. You married down. And don't think you're going to change him or build him up. Men don't look to you for counsel and growth; they go to the men before them. A wise woman can use her womanly gifts to help him move the way he should, but you are not going to sit him down, teach him the scriptures and make him ready for camp.

precepts.why: Being cast about is what a city without walls looks like. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” You see the signs and you hear them in his speech and his daily decision making: he doesn't know if he's coming or going, one minute it's this, the next minute it's that. That is the man you're going to follow and expect to make sure everything is taken care of? You'll mess around and be homeless, sister. He's unstable, and he is not ready yet.

sense.text:
Another sign. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” Ask the brother if he gives alms to the school, and most will say yes. Come to find out he doesn't, and he's barely making ends meet, barely able to feed himself. You think he's ready for a wife, and you're going to step in a situation like, save a negro? No. He's not.

No father should give his daughter to a man who cannot financially sustain her. He doesn't have to be rich, but she needs a roof over her head, food, a place to bathe, and safety. A spot at his cousin's house is not stability; if the cousin says go, you're homeless. Getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, you can't reach him and he calls tomorrow because he had to get on the Wi-Fi: these are the signs. If you see them early, congratulations, you spotted him. Now are you going to play dumb because you like the idea of being married, the congratulations and the big family, or wise up, not sell yourself short and follow counsel?

Spot the signs when he is led by lust. Some of you think you're just gorgeous and have that effect on people. Maybe he's just nasty. “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men.” Does he understand this?

“Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.” Denying is an action: to deny ungodliness he has to be working to make sure he is not in the midst of sin.

How does he show a lust issue? Porn, social media. It's eleven at night and he lets her know, I'm naked right now. He put that thought in her mind. You have to see through the innuendos: he's setting the mood, lining you up. What you got on right now? Let's go live real quick. The devil upped the game.

When you see that, sister, get the hell off the phone: holler at me when you've got clothes on. Put him in his place, and he will know she's not one of them, I probably got a strike. Sometimes that is a complete deal breaker. And when it gets out that she ended it because she wouldn't let him drag her into sin, brothers will hear she is about the Lord. But if it comes out that y'all were having phone sex, the next one will hear that too and you'll attract a brother just like that again. Break the cycle.

Another sign. “Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish.” Ask questions about his conduct and speak to leadership. How does he handle correction? How does he deal with being told to do something? If he doesn't like taking correction from the men over him, know for sure he has a problem with God. The scripture gave us order and structure, and whoever disrespects those over him disrespects the order God set up. If he has a problem with God, who the hell are you? A man who cannot take correction will be hell to pay if you get with him.

Signs that a woman is a liability and not an asset: attention seeking, no accountability, emotions she cannot manage, disrespect when upset, materialism, no respect for boundaries, poor character, neediness and jealousy, insecurity, control, no privacy, selfishness. And it goes both ways. You inherit all of your spouse's problems.

“Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.” This is the righteous order God set up among us: we fall in line and deal with each other according to the scriptures. Anybody who has a problem with that has something wrong with their relationship with God. Security tells someone to sit over there and they catch an attitude: why me? Stop. Follow instructions. You should never have a problem with protocol and instruction. Brothers, if she is one of those sisters who always has something to say, red flag.

“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” The same authority Christ has over the church, the husband has over the wife. Look for women who understand that. They respect order, there is no back and forth, and they support whatever leadership puts in place.

As Christ was the head of the church, he set up apostles and deacons, a structure in order so everything runs the way it's supposed to. A woman who understands structure understands authority and that she herself has to be in line with it. If she doesn't, brothers, do not marry her. And the same with brothers: if he comes to you complaining about what the captain said, and he never talked to the captain about it, he is trying to use you to murmur. Run, sisters. A person who doesn't respect order and structure will not respect the order and structure in the house.

“It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman.” The signs of a brawling woman: she's contentious, she doesn't follow orders, everything is a fight. Everybody has a representative while proving, so watch how she deals with the body, how she takes correction from a brother when she is put in an office, how she deals with leadership and with the senior sisters telling her when she's wrong. Ask who her friends are and who is in her circle. If she is comfortable challenging you consistently over any and everything, she has that spirit on her. Pay attention to the signs, brothers, or you'll be up in the corner on the roof with a beer, not wanting to go downstairs.

There is a balance. You don't want a wife who tells you everything is great all the time; she is supposed to say something when she sees what you don't, so the house goes the right direction. But not trusting your judgment and your leadership all the time is a problem, and you can see those early signs in a person who is always going back and forth with you.

“And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand.” Make sure the foundation is not sand. The way you begin your marriage and your relationship affects the rest of it: the probability of it being successful and being in Christ is affected by how you started.

That does not mean those who did a back-door marriage are doomed forever. You have to make the best of your situation, and it can get better. The point is to spare people the hardship that comes from doing things unadvisedly, without counsel, because they were hard-headed. Just think what life would be like if you didn't have to go through it.

“And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.” The rain and floods are the problems; the winds are the tribulations. Anything we do that is not rooted and founded on Christ is going to fall. Be mindful, take the counsel, and do not ignore the red flags. Love should not blind wisdom, and if something feels wrong now it won't magically fix itself after marriage.

Choose wisely. “O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel! O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honour! Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of God is their glory.”

This is why the Lord tells you to wear down the steps. Nobody in this room has an excuse to say, I don't have anybody I can talk to about these things. You're a damn liar. There are men here who have gone through it and senior sisters who have dealt with it, who can help you make the right decision if you are honest and open about what you are experiencing.

And it isn't always doom and gloom. Sometimes you don't need to end the proving; there may be something in you that you don't see, that you are battling, and a person can help you conquer it so you can continue the proving process.

“Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart; that thy soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone.” Don't lift yourself up on the counsel of your own heart. That kind of thinking, not seeking counsel and not trying to find out, has destroyed so many people.

“Thou shalt eat up thy leaves, and lose thy fruit, and leave thyself as a dry tree.” So many have fallen victim to their own counsel and their own minds, thinking they have it all figured out. You don't have the answers. You need to seek counsel.

Imagine driving on the wrong side of the highway with an officer telling you to turn around, and you say, you don't know what you're talking about. Boom, you're dead.

“Let reason go before every enterprize.” Before every enterprise, make sure it is sound and makes sense, that thought has been put into it. Never do anything on a whim, piecing things together with half-assed research. “And counsel before every action.” Before you make a move, before you seal the deal, get counsel and find out if this is what you should do, and you will save yourself a whole lot of heartache.
